overall_summary: Crypto tone is cautious and mixed after Bitcoin's bounce to seventy-eight thousand, with heavy spot ETF outflows and Binance hack-related withdrawals still pressuring flows. Softer dollar and lower yields give some support, while Moscow's planned listings add a constructive note. Traders stay focused on jobs data, Fed odds, and Iran-related oil risk before taking a clear side.
key_points: ETF outflows top one billion dollars
Moscow Exchange to list BTC ETH
Jobs data and Iran strikes keep risk mixed

items.title: BTC V-Recovers to $78K After Democratic Midterm Dip
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly crashed to a seven-week low near seventy-five thousand six hundred dollars as Democrats swept control of both the House and Senate. It then staged a sharp V-shaped rebound back above seventy-eight thousand as election uncertainty cleared. Traders should watch because a less crypto-friendly Congress could slow bills like the CLARITY Act, even if the immediate political risk premium faded and roughly three hundred million in longs got liquidated.
items.impact: Short-term relief bounce; longer regulatory drag possible

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.16B Over Three Sessions
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another one hundred fifteen million dollars in net outflows on Tuesday, extending a three-day streak that totals about one point one six billion. BlackRock’s IBIT led with heavy redemptions, including its biggest single-day hit since June. This matters because persistent institutional selling removes a key bid under price even as Bitcoin rebounded from the election low.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure on BTC from institutions

items.title: Binance Sees Billions in Net Outflows After $6.3B Hack
items.summary: Customers pulled a net four point seven to five point three billion dollars from Binance after it restored withdrawals following the record six point three billion dollar hack linked to North Korea. The exchange says it has covered most losses from its own funds and that hourly flows are starting to stabilize. Traders care because large exchange outflows can flood the market with supply and keep risk appetite suppressed.
items.impact: Exchange confidence hit and potential spot selling

items.title: Block Faces $764M DOJ Deal as Bitcoin Profits Halve
items.summary: Jack Dorsey’s Block reached a tentative deferred prosecution agreement that could cost about seven hundred sixty-four million dollars to settle a Justice Department probe into Cash App anti-money-laundering controls. At the same time its bitcoin ecosystem gross profit dropped fifty percent after fee cuts, though the company still added a modest amount of bitcoin to its holdings. This is relevant as a major bitcoin-facing public company faces a large compliance hit and thinner trading margins.
items.impact: Company-specific overhang with limited direct BTC price force

items.title: Moscow Exchange to List BTC, ETH, USDT on Dec. 1
items.summary: Russia’s largest exchange plans to open pilot trading in bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT starting December first on its existing stock-market infrastructure. Non-qualified investors face tests and annual purchase caps while the venue and its clearer remain under Western sanctions. It expands regulated access in a large market and could add incremental demand even if global liquidity impact stays limited at first.
items.impact: Incremental adoption and new regulated venue demand

items.title: Near $300M Long Liquidations as BTC Tests 7-Week Low
items.summary: The election-night slide under seventy-six thousand dollars wiped out roughly two hundred eighty-eight to three hundred million dollars in leveraged long positions across crypto in twenty-four hours. Most of the pain hit bitcoin longs as price tagged the fifty-week moving average. Traders should note the flush reduces crowded leverage and can set up cleaner moves once the dust settles, but failed defense of that average risks deeper downside.
items.impact: Leverage reset; support test remains key for next direction

items.title: Democrats Sweep Midterms, Control Congress
items.summary: Democrats have taken control of both the House and Senate in the 2026 midterms, delivering a setback to President Trump's agenda. Markets reacted overnight with the dollar sliding, Treasury yields falling, and gold climbing as investors priced in less fiscal stimulus and potential tighter AI regulation. Traders should care because gridlock typically eases long-end yield pressure and can support risk assets including crypto via a softer dollar and reduced rate-hike urgency.
items.impact: Weaker DXY and lower yields supportive for Bitcoin

items.title: Eurozone Inflation Hits 4% Three-Year High
items.summary: Eurozone flash CPI rose to 4.0 percent year-on-year in October from 3.8 percent, matching forecasts, driven by energy prices up 20.8 percent. Core inflation held steady at 2.5 percent. This keeps December ECB hike odds elevated near 84 percent. Crypto traders watch it because tighter European policy can firm the euro and weigh on global liquidity, though the main driver today remains US politics.
items.impact: Supports ECB tightening; limited immediate BTC hit with USD weak

items.title: JOLTS Job Openings Surge to 7.523 Million
items.summary: September JOLTS showed job openings jumping 333,000 to 7.523 million, well above the 7.1 million forecast, with August revised higher. Quits rose and layoffs fell, pointing to a still-resilient labor market. This data, released Tuesday, reinforces high odds of a December Fed hike and keeps the focus on Friday's NFP. Strong labor keeps the Fed hawkish, which is a headwind for risk assets until yields fully price it.
items.impact: Firms Fed hike bets, potential yield support and USD bid

items.title: ISM Services PMI Due Today at 10am ET
items.summary: The key ISM Services PMI for October is scheduled for release at 10:00 AM Eastern, with consensus around 54.8 versus 54.9 prior. Services dominate the US economy, so a big miss or beat moves yields, the dollar, and Fed expectations ahead of Friday jobs. Traders should watch the employment and prices components closely for signals on labor tightness and inflation persistence that feed directly into Bitcoin volatility.
items.impact: High-impact data; surprise could swing DXY and risk sentiment

items.title: Dollar Weakens, 10-Year Yield Drops Near 4.92%
items.summary: The DXY fell as much as 0.5-0.6 percent toward multi-week lows near 101.3-101.4 while the 10-year Treasury yield declined several basis points to around 4.92 percent. The move followed the Democratic midterm sweep and safe-haven flows. A softer greenback and lower real yields are classic tailwinds for Bitcoin and gold, though any rebound in yields on strong data could reverse it quickly.
items.impact: Lower DXY and yields typically lift crypto prices

items.title: ADP Jobs Today, NFP Friday; Fed Hike Odds High
items.summary: ADP private payrolls for October land today with consensus near 69,000 after 90,000 prior, serving as a warm-up for Friday's full Employment Situation report. Markets still price roughly 75-80 percent odds of a December Fed rate hike after recent strong labor prints. Crypto traders need to stay positioned for volatility around these releases because a hot number would reinforce higher-for-longer rates and pressure Bitcoin.
items.impact: Data path will dictate near-term rate and USD direction

items.title: Democrats Sweep Midterms, Seize Congress from Trump
items.summary: Democrats flipped both the House and Senate in a historic blue wave, winning deep-red states like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina. Voters cited high prices from tariffs and the Iran war as key reasons for rejecting Republicans. For traders this means gridlock ahead, which often supports risk assets by limiting major new spending or policy shocks, though investigations of the administration could create noise.
items.impact: Gridlock may stabilize markets; reduced Trump free rein on tariffs and foreign policy

items.title: US Strikes Iran Qeshm Island Near Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: US forces hit Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in limited defensive strikes after IRGC fired on American aircraft and threatened shipping. Officials called it part of quiet recent operations while Trump downplays full war and pushes diplomacy. Oil traders should watch closely because Hormuz remains a chokepoint for global crude, and any escalation keeps energy prices elevated and risk assets under pressure.
items.impact: Heightens oil supply risk and geopolitical premium on crude

items.title: Trump Ends Annual $4 Billion Military Aid to Israel
items.summary: President Trump announced a deal with Netanyahu to halt roughly four billion dollars in yearly US military aid by year-end, saying Israel no longer needs it. The move removes a political talking point for Democrats and shifts the alliance toward arms sales. Markets may see this as reducing US fiscal outlays but it injects uncertainty into Middle East security dynamics already strained by the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Mixed fiscal signal; potential shift in regional alliance costs and tensions

items.title: US-Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks Set for Abu Dhabi
items.summary: The United States will mediate trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, following recent envoy meetings. Zelenskyy hopes it opens a path to direct leader talks while the Kremlin confirmed participation. De-escalation progress here would ease energy infrastructure risks from Ukrainian drones and support broader risk-on sentiment for crypto and equities.
items.impact: Potential de-escalation lowers energy and geopolitical risk premiums

items.title: Russian Strike Kills Dozens at Ukraine Aid Center
items.summary: A Russian bombing hit an aid distribution center and shelter in Zaporizhzhia, killing at least 33 people with dozens missing. This comes as peace talks are scheduled and follows earlier ceasefire pauses. Persistent civilian targeting keeps the conflict hot and can spill into energy markets via attacks on Russian refining, weighing on risk appetite until talks show real progress.
items.impact: Sustains war risk and potential energy infrastructure disruptions

items.title: Oil Volatile Near $104 as Iran Diplomacy Hopes Clash with Strikes
items.summary: Brent crude hovered around one hundred three to one hundred four dollars after a sharp drop on peace talk signals, then rebounded modestly on the Qeshm strikes and midterm uncertainty. Flows through Hormuz remain disrupted and diesel prices stay elevated. Crypto traders care because sticky energy costs feed inflation, rate expectations, and overall risk sentiment.
items.impact: Keeps inflation and energy volatility elevated pending diplomatic resolution
